problem: Retailer price collection runs inside the web process, so a slow retailer delays user requests and a restart loses in-flight collection.
outcome: Price collection runs as a separate scheduled worker with its own durable queue, so user requests stay fast and a restart resumes collection.
intended_user_value: The owner keeps a responsive product and complete price history even when a retailer is slow or the host restarts.
scope: Move retailer collection out of the request path into a scheduled worker.
Persist the collection queue so work resumes after restart.
out_of_scope: Real-time push updates to the browser.
requirements: Collection work is enqueued durably and processed outside the request path.
A restart resumes pending collection without duplicating recorded prices.
Collection failures are recorded and retried with a bounded policy.
acceptance_criteria: A user request completes without waiting for retailer collection.
Restarting the worker mid-run resumes pending items exactly once.
A failing retailer is retried within the bounded policy and then recorded as failed.
constraints: No additional recurring hosting cost beyond the existing plan.
risks: Queue durability choice affects future hosting portability.
Exactly-once recording depends on idempotent write keys.

adr_disposition.reason: Introduces a new long-lived runtime and durable queue ownership; ADR-0010 records the decision and is linked before implementation proceeds.

owner_decisions: Accept a background worker rather than extending request timeouts.

source.summary: Conversation exposed a material architecture decision; the ADR was created and linked before implementation.
